content: The mRNA-decapping enzyme 1A is a protein encoded by the DCP1A gene in humans. This enzyme plays a critical role in the process of mRNA decapping, which is an essential step in both general and regulated mRNA degradation. The protein functions as a decapping enzyme and forms a decapping complex in conjunction with another decapping enzyme. This complex interacts with the nonsense-mediated decay factor hUpf1 and can be recruited to mRNAs that contain premature termination codons, facilitating their degradation. Additionally, this protein is involved in the TGF-beta signaling pathway. The DCP1A protein has been demonstrated to interact with DCP2, another decapping enzyme, as well as with UPF1, a key factor in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Furthermore, it has been shown to interact with GW182, a marker of P-bodies, which are cytoplasmic structures involved in mRNA processing and decay.
